pr_body:
I recently discovered in #45162 that the initializers for multiple
databases are not working as intended. The
`config.active_record.database_selector` and other selector config options
work fine if they are called from `config/application.rb` or from
`config/environments/production.rb`. However when called from config
initalizers, the initializer from acitve record is loaded _before_ the
multi-db initialzier. This means that options never gets set and the
middleware never gets installed.

While it's nice to have the `config.active_record` keys for setting this
configuration, it's not really necessary, so I've solved this by using
the initializer to install the middleware directly like this:

Database Selector Before:

```ruby
Rails.application.configure do
  config.active_record.database_selector = { delay: 2.seconds }
  config.active_record.database_resolver = ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector::Resolver
  config.active_record.database_resolver_context = ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector::Resolver::Session
end
```

Database Selector After:

```ruby
Rails.application.configure do
  options = { delay: 2.seconds }
  resolver = ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector::Resolver
  context = ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector::Resolver::Session

  config.middleware.use ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector, resolver, context, options
end
```

Shard Selector Before:

```ruby
Rails.application.configure do
  config.active_record.shard_selector = { lock: true }
  config.active_record.shard_resolver = ->(request) { Tenant.find_by!(host: request.host).shard }
end
```

Shard Selector After:

```ruby
Rails.application.configure do
  options = { lock: true }
  resolver = ->(request) { Tenant.find_by!(host: request.host).shard }

  config.middleware.use ActiveRecord::Middleware::ShardSelector, resolver, options
end
```

The changes here are:

1) Raise if anyone is using the old keys. I'd love to deprecate this
but it's straight up not working so it needs to be removed instead.
2) Update the multi_db generator file to use the new method.
3) Update the documentation to use the new method.

This is going to be the least fun for applications that are using these
keys in their `application.rb` or env configs already. But since I can't
distinguish between where these are loaded the best course of action is
to just remove them and raise an error pushing them in the right
direction. I don't love this especially since it will need to be
backported to a release, 7.0, but I don't see a better option. I tried a
bunch of different ways to get these configs to load on time but nothing
worked. I had hope `after_initialize` would work, but the middleware
still isn't installed on time.

Closes #45162
pr_comments:
> But since I can't distinguish between where these are loaded the best course of action is to just remove them and raise an error pushing them in the right direction.

I think you can. If the config exists [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/0adc2347d90482315c7c045a7431a03d30a59332/activerecord/lib/active_record/railtie.rb#L98) then it was added in `application.rb` or an environment config. You'd need to use `config.active_record.delete(:database_selector)` instead of how it's currently written. Then, if the config exists at your current deprecation warning, you know it was added in an initializer.

This is speculative but I'm fairly confident about it, if you like I can try and add these changes + the test to a branch targeting this one?

ps. I'm 👍 👍 💯   on this solution in general, just thinking about how to minimise the pain for upgrading apps. Particularly if you only have `config.active_record.database_selector` set in `environment/production.rb`, adding something that raises on boot could be a really bad time.

> I think you can. If the config exists [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/0adc2347d90482315c7c045a7431a03d30a59332/activerecord/lib/active_record/railtie.rb#L98) then it was added in application.rb or an environment config. You'd need to use config.active_record.delete(:database_selector) instead of how it's currently written. Then, if the config exists at your current deprecation warning, you know it was added in an initializer.

You were right, thanks! I've deprecated the ones called from application.rb and env configs but am raising for ones called outside those two places.

I also added a test to ensure the middleware is being installed.

Awesome, thanks for checking.
I guess the only risk now is if someone's set this in an initializer, but only `if Rails.env.production?`, at which it will still raise on boot in production where previously it did nothing. But I don't really see how (other than with release notes / changelogs) we can prevent that 🤷

Closing in favor of https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/45368. If I move these configs to the Railtie, everything works because the Railties middleware installation is loaded after multi_db is loaded.

issue_context.title: config/initializers/multi_db doesn't work
issue_context.body:
It doesn't insert the database selector middleware, because the railtie which inserts it has already run by the time the initializer is run.

## Repro 

[See repo here.](https://github.com/nate-at-gusto/multidb-dont-work)

```
bin/rails test test/integration/replica_test.rb 
```
comments:
Related: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/44996

If that PR isn't accepted, then `config.after_initializer` might fix it, here: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/b24c44159c4dc5904c78d61b57a8728846d453a9/activerecord/lib/active_record/railtie.rb#L98

In the meantime, moving the config to `application.rb` (like it was before https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/43796) definitely works.

I know that we discussed in chat that order of config initializers has been a problem for awhile but I am 100% sure I tested this in an app when I implemented it. This leads me to believe something else changed between 6.1 and 7.0 that is causing all these initializers to now not work. 😕

> This leads me to believe something else changed between 6.1 and 7.0 that is causing all these initializers to now not work. 😕

I haven't dug into it much but I have a feeling https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42499 was working around the same regression.

Trying to bisect this, but not having much luck yet.

`railties/test/application/configuration_test.rb`:

```ruby
    test "can get multi-db middleware from initializer" do
      app_file "config/initializers/multi_db.rb", <<-RUBY
        Rails.application.configure do
          config.active_record.database_selector = { delay: 2.seconds }
        end
      RUBY

      app "development"

      assert_includes Rails.application.config.middleware.map(&:name), "ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector"
    end

    test "can get multi-db middleware from application.rb" do
      add_to_config <<-RUBY
        config.active_record.database_selector = { delay: 2.seconds }
      RUBY

      app "development"

      assert_includes Rails.application.config.middleware.map(&:name), "ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector"
    end
```

On both `main` and `6-1-stable` the first test fails and the second test passes. I'm having some trouble getting `6-0-stable` to build atm so can't confirm if it works there.

I did some poking around. I don't know if this helps at all but i want to brain dump so I can wrap up for the day. The main interesting thing is that the order that railties get evaluated in is defined here https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/55cee0331e1af4fb517291108045f39cb19dfd41/railties/lib/rails/application.rb#L558

This is the order on Rails 6.1, on 7 it's basically the same: `["I18n::Railtie", "ActiveSupport::Railtie", "ActionDispatch::Railtie", "ActiveModel::Railtie", "ActionController::Railtie", "ActiveRecord::Railtie", "GlobalID::Railtie", "ActiveJob::Railtie", "ActionMailer::Railtie", "Rails::TestUnitRailtie", "Sprockets::Railtie", "ActionView::Railtie", "ActiveStorage::Engine", "ActionCable::Engine", "ActionMailbox::Engine", "ActionText::Engine", "Turbolinks::Engine", "Webpacker::Engine", "AppTemplate::Application"]`

So all the railties, and then all the engines, as defined [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/55cee0331e1af4fb517291108045f39cb19dfd41/railties/lib/rails/engine/railties.rb#L10).

https://gist.github.com/ghiculescu/8d36b09402daff400d3786f89964c7ca lists each railtie/engine and which initializers it adds. My debug code was

```ruby
    def railties_initializers(current) #:nodoc:
      initializers = []
      puts "railties is #{railties.to_a.map(&:class).map(&:name)}"
      puts "ordered_railties is #{ordered_railties.reverse.flatten.map(&:class).map(&:name)}"
      ordered_railties.reverse.flatten.each do |r|
        puts "r is #{r}"
        if r == self
          puts "adding #{current.map(&:name)}"
          initializers += current
        else
          puts "adding #{r.initializers.map(&:name)}"
          initializers += r.initializers
        end
      end
      initializers
    end
```

What's interesting is that `load_config_initializers` is not explicitly called by any of the railties. It is called basically as a side effect of all the engines. As a result it is called relatively late.

It seems to me like it should probably be called at a specified point, not randomly halfway through the loading of the frameworks.

I spent a long time on this today trying to determine when and how certain configs broke and the only thing I've come up with is that certain config initializations have broken since at least 6.0 and in Ruby 2.6 to to 3.0. This initializer predates 6.0 so I was testing with others that have been around for awhile.

For example calling `Rails.application.config.active_record.use_schema_cache_dump = false` in 6.1 and 6.0 raises an error that `use_schema_cache_dump` is undefined. I also see this if I set up the multi_db initializer - `database_selector` is undefined.

I can see why this is happening, the initializer in the Railtie runs before the initializer is loaded from config. `options` is never set so nothing else is set either. I attempted to use `after_initialize` with the Railtie and that didn't improve the situation.

I think the best course going forward is to drop the `config.active_record.database_selector` initializer that installs the middleware in the Railtie, and install it directly with the config initializer. PR incoming.

I've come to the conclusion that no one noticed before because we were using initializers less for this kind of thing. That's the only reasonable explanation I can come up with since it doesn't look like anything changed. That or this particular issue isn't related to the other issues we're seeing.

This is what I've come up with as a fix #45353

It has the unfortunate side effect that applications using these in places where they do work (application.rb) will still throw a deprecation warning.

Decided to fix this differently in #https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/45368. Backported to 7-0-stable. It will be in the next release. In the mean time calling these intializers from config/application.rb or config/environments works fine.
Thanks @eileencodes this just saved me from a long, miserable 2-3 days of troubleshooting, lol.

review_comments: Is it worth adding a test similar to https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/45162#issuecomment-1145424714 to ensure this works as expected?
Probably but I am not excited about how hard that's going to be 😓 I'm not entirely sure it's possible without a huge amount of setup.

Actually - I think I just need to test the middleware is installed and can assume that if it is then everything else works. Active Record is already testing the functionality of the middleware itself. I was assuming this was going to be hard because of booting a server, running requests, and checking the connection, but we don't need to do all that.
Oh yeah that's what I meant. You could just copy-paste those tests and change the config lines.
